summary: Gemini 3.5 Flash is a retired Google card for a Gemini 3 Flash successor that adds thinking levels and reports better results on several coding, agentic, multimodal, and long-context tasks. Much of the short card delegates architecture, training data, known limitations, acceptable-use, and broader risk information to the Gemini 3 Flash and Gemini 3.1 Pro cards.

capabilities.text: Gemini 3.5 Flash is framed as a natively multimodal reasoning model in the Gemini 3 series.
The model builds on Gemini 3 Flash and adds thinking levels for task-dependent behavior.
The card lists text, images, audio, and video as input types, with context up to 1M tokens.
Outputs are text and can reach 64K tokens.
Distribution channels include Gemini App, Gemini Enterprise App, Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Google AI Studio, Gemini API, Google Search AI Mode, and Google Antigravity.
Google names agentic workflows, coding tasks, and multi-week enterprise processes as intended use cases.

evaluations.context: Agentic terminal coding on the Terminus-2 harness.
Multi-step workflows using MCP; highest row value shown.
Information synthesis from complex charts without tools.
Multimodal understanding and reasoning without tools.
Academic reasoning across full-set text and multimodal tasks.

safety_findings.text: Automated safety testing versus Gemini 3 Flash reports text-to-text safety down 3.9%, multilingual safety down 2.6%, image-to-text safety unchanged, tone up 8.9%, and unjustified refusals up 0.8% with a non-egregious note.
Google characterizes the development results as better safety and tone than Gemini 3 Flash while maintaining low unjustified refusals.
Manual red teams found child-safety launch thresholds met, similar or improved content safety versus Gemini 3 Flash, and no egregious concerns in broader probing.
For Frontier Safety, Google relies on Gemini 3.1 Pro results and says Gemini 3.5 Flash is also unlikely to reach critical capability levels.
Extra cyber testing found Gemini 3.5 Flash below the cyber critical capability level.

limitations.text: Known limitations are not restated in detail; the card points readers to the Gemini 3 Flash model card.
Acceptable-use, safety evaluation approach, and safety policy details are also delegated to the Gemini 3 Flash card.
Capability-benchmark methodology is referred to an external methodology page rather than explained in this short card.
The safety table is automated development testing rather than human evaluation or red-teaming.
Google cautions that its refined automated safety evaluations make these safety results unsuitable for direct comparison with older Gemini model-card numbers.
Risk and mitigation details are mostly deferred to the Gemini 3.1 Pro model card.

practical_implications.text: GitHub retired Gemini 3.5 Flash on 2026-10-02; the remaining bullets are for historical comparison and for understanding the successor model's lineage.
Its benchmark mix helps explain why later Flash models emphasized terminal coding, MCP-style workflows, and long-context use.
For old outputs produced by this model, re-check factual claims and code because this short card does not restate the detailed limitations it inherits from Gemini 3 Flash.
The mild unjustified-refusal increase means historical comparisons should separate safety improvements from potential answer-availability changes.
The cyber testing note reinforces that agent tool access should remain constrained even when a model is positioned as a faster Flash variant.

coverage_notes: This digest uses pages 2-3 for model identity, modalities, and distribution; page 4 for the benchmark chart; page 5 for intended use and delegated limitations; and pages 6-7 for safety, red teaming, Frontier Safety, and risk references. The card is dedicated to Gemini 3.5 Flash, but it sends readers to Gemini 3 Flash and Gemini 3.1 Pro for many underlying details. The external evaluation methodology page is mentioned but not summarized beyond the card.
